reason: The text demonstrates the leaders (Moses and Aaron) and the people working together toward the common goal of the Exodus from Egypt. Moses and Aaron receive divine instructions and direct the people, while the people actively respond and execute the commands: 'And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses' (וּבְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עָשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה) and 'all the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron: so did they.' The people are not passive but actively participate—preparing unleavened bread, gathering possessions, and participating in the coordinated departure. This represents cooperation and coordinated action toward a shared objective, demonstrating leaders and people working together, even within a hierarchical command structure.
